en: The Therāpadāna: The Chapter on the Great Retinue (Mahāparivāravagga) 5. The Apadāna of the Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya [Verse 1] "O Bhikkhu, you who possess such a beautiful form, With a face like the full moon, And a body adorned with the marks of a great man— Whose son are you? [Verse 2] "I am not the son of anyone in the world; I have no father or mother. I am the son of the Dhamma, born from the Dhamma; I am the heir to the Dhamma. [Verse 3] "You are truly a son of the Dhamma, Born from the Dhamma and nurtured by the Dhamma. Tell me, O Bhikkhu, what was your former deed, By which you have attained such beauty? [Verse 4] "In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a monk named Suvaṇṇapupphiya. I offered a golden flower to the Buddha, And because of that merit, I have attained this state. [Verse 5] "Having seen the golden flower offered by me, The Teacher Kassapa spoke these words: ‘In the future, after a hundred thousand aeons, This one shall become a Buddha named Gotama. [Verse 6] "Because of that offering of a golden flower, I have been reborn in a noble family. I have attained the state of a Stream-enterer, And I shall reach the end of suffering. [Verse 7] "Having heard the Elder’s words, The King was filled with joy. He bowed his head at the Elder’s feet And departed from that place. [Verse 8] "The Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya, Having fulfilled his duties, passed away. Reborn in the realm of Tusita, He dwells there in bliss. [Verse 9] "Thus did the Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya, Through his former deeds, attain such glory. May all beings, having heard this account, Strive to perform meritorious deeds. [Verse 10] "This is the Apadāna of the Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya, The fifth in the Chapter on the Great Retinue. May it bring peace and prosperity to all."
“The Blessed One named Vipassī,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
was seated before the multitude of people.”
He taught the deathless state.
Having heard the Dhamma from that peerless leader of bipeds, I—
I offered four golden flowers to the Buddha;
it was covered with gold.
To whatever extent the assembly was gathered then,
there was the radiance of the Buddha and a golden luster;
a vast light prevailed.
With an uplifted mind, joyful,
filled with rapture, and with palms joined in reverence, he inspired them with gladness.
Bringing happiness in this very life.
Having entreated the Fully Awakened One and paid homage to him of excellent vows,
Having generated joy,
I returned to my own abode.
Having entered my abode, I—
I recollected the Best of Buddhas;
through that clarity of mind,
I was reborn in Tusita.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I offered that flower,
I do not know any state of woe.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
there were sixteen kings named Nemisammata.
In the forty-fourth aeon from now,
there were wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Suvaṇṇapupphiya, the fifth.
